findings.reason: the node's only negative control is false at base, so its gate would pass on unchanged code and measure nothing.
findings.text: §23's negative control, "a churn of an input that does not change the answer (a pointer rewrite with the same worktree)", does not reproduce at base: `_held_records_signature` (`reckon/crew/obligations.py:2236-2242`) keys the live pointers on exactly `(run_id, worktree)`, so a rewrite carrying the same worktree leaves `live_signature`, `registry_signature` and `ledger_signature` all unchanged and `file_memo.memoized_key` (`:2203-2207`) serves the previous answer — the base refresh does not repeat the work, so the head assertion cannot fail there. If instead the rewrite changes `run_id`, the answer can change, so it is not the control the plan describes.

findings.reason: the worker either narrows the assertion to the work inside `_held_worktree_records_read` or discards the pointer read from the key, and the plan currently forces neither choice.
findings.text: §23's head clause, "a second refresh with no change performs none of the underlying listing or stat work", cannot hold even at head as the deliverable is written: every call recomputes the key, and `_held_records_signature` reads the live pointers through `_live_pointers` → `runs.list_live` (a directory listing plus one read per pointer) while `_held_worktree_records` also stats each held path at `obligations.py:2208`; a key built on "the pointers that name them" therefore cannot avoid either.

findings.reason: the control names the one edit the base already ignores, so the gate's failure mode at base is unreachable and the measure cannot discriminate.
findings.text: §24's negative control, "an edit to a plan with no queued request between the two calls makes the second rebuild the roadmap", is false at base: `slugs` is built only from queued pointers (`reckon/crew/queue_order.py:56-60`) and `_named_plan_signature` stats only those plan files (`:23-35`), so an edit to a plan with no queued request leaves the signature identical and `_PRIORITY_KEYS` serves the cached keys (`:62-64`) — the base does not rebuild.

findings.reason: a worker implementing the deliverable fails its own head assertion, and one satisfying the assertion keeps rebuilding on every touch and delivers nothing.
findings.text: §24's head assertion, "touching a plan file makes the next call rebuild it", contradicts its own deliverable, which requires that "prose that does not change a section's state, waits or sprint" not invalidate the keys: a touch that changes no semantic field must not rebuild at head, so the assertion fails at head for exactly the edit the section asks the worker to absorb.

findings.reason: a worker following the deliverable narrows the wrong input and either keeps the per-tick miss or serves a stale held-tree answer after a release.
findings.text: §23's Why and Deliverable name the wrong churn source and then drop the real one: the base key already excludes every pointer field except `run_id` and `worktree`, so "churn in other pointer fields no longer misses the cache" describes a property it already has, while the input that actually moves on most ticks is the merged ledger file's stat identity (`obligations.py:2232`), and the Deliverable's named inputs — "the worktree trees and the pointers that name them" — omit the ledger, whose content genuinely can change the answer when a promotion record releases a tree.

findings.reason: the worker given this text implements a clause that is already true and is left to invent the real change, including its cost, which the plan should name.
findings.text: §24's Deliverable leads with "an edit to a plan with no queued request … does not invalidate them", a property the base already holds, and never states the mechanism its own measure needs — keying on parsed section state rather than the file's stat identity — nor the per-tick plan parse that key implies.
